notes: Portrait, straight-on, three shelves of a second-hand bookshop in soft indoor light, no glare. English throughout. A wire easel with a handwritten card ('I am always interested in Buying Books') stands in front of the middle shelf and hides the lower half of a dozen spines, and the shelf above cuts the tops of the top row. Series: the four Brontë volumes bottom right are labelled by volume title. Partial: On Deconstruction (Culler, only '...ruction' clear), Jacques Derrida: Opening Lines ('Jacques' cut), A Political Treatise (Spinoza, Dover, first half of the title hidden), Freud's Women (only 'FREUD' shows behind the easel), An Introduction to Wittgenstein's Tractatus (start hidden by the card), The Origins of Political Order (Fukuyama, only 'OF POLITICAL ORDER' below the card), How to Stop Worrying and Start Living (Carnegie, yellow spine crossed by the easel leg), Arthurian Literature by Women (cut by the left frame edge), Cat's Eye (Atwood, only 'CA' visible), Time's Arrow (Amis, only 'TIMES' visible). Left out: the green and blue spines top centre with worn or torn labels, the two dark Wittgenstein volumes whose titles sit behind the card, the 'VII' volume and the small 'ets' book, the Kevin D. Murray and Jean-Paul Sartre spines (author only), a book showing only 'of Ideas', the ochre spine with Margaret Atwood's name at the top of the bottom shelf, and the draft's 'The End of History and the Last Man', which is not on the shelf (the Fukuyama here is The Origins of Political Order). Drafted by claude-sonnet-5 (extraction 89), verified by an agent.
